audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may embed a future-period commodity hedge loss
audit_findings.magnitude: $423.161m filed 2025 unallocated commodity-derivative loss, equal to 41.7% of the $1,015.6m anchor; the cited $491.0m is a year-over-year cost-of-sales effect, not a standalone 2025 loss
audit_findings.mechanism: A timing-related derivative loss retained in 2025 OE depresses the anchor and every projected year; later recognition of the underlying commodity cost could then count the economics twice.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, in addition to higher commodity costs, our cost of sales increased compared to the same period of 2024 as a result of $491.0 million of unfavorable mark-to-market activity on our commodity derivative instruments intended to economically hedge future years’ commodity purchases.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial derivative timing effects, but the record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation retained or normalized them. Because the filed unallocated amount is large relative to the anchor, the unresolved treatment is reasonably capable of materially changing value. Any normalization must preserve the ultimate commodity purchase cost.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 OE line by line to net income, operating cash flow and the $423.161m unallocated derivative adjustment; rerun all scenarios only for the after-tax timing amount actually retained, while retaining commodity costs when the related inventory is sold.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter ignores a late-year acquisition represented for only six weeks in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified OE contribution; filed final purchase consideration $810.150m, equal to 5.3% of $15,235m base equity value or $4.00 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Only post-November 18 LesserEvil earnings enter the 2025 OE anchor, although subsequent operations and acquisition-related assets and financing cover the entire acquired business.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 18, 2025, we completed the acquisition of LesserEvil, LLC (“LesserEvil”), previously a privately held company that produces and sells organic popcorn and puffed snack products to retailers and distributors in the United States and Canada, which complements Hershey’s existing product portfolio and brings additional manufacturing capacity.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-period perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Materiality cannot be established because LesserEvil's standalone OE, integration costs and normalized maintenance investment are not disclosed. The acquisition is large enough to require resolution, but its contribution could be positive or negative; 2026 salty-snacks sales growth does not establish its OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain LesserEvil's audited pre-acquisition 2025 results and 2026 standalone revenue, operating cash flow, taxes and maintenance-capex requirements; construct a supported full-year OE contribution and rerun the anchor and scenarios if material.

audit_findings.title: LesserEvil earnout is a claim ahead of common equity not shown in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum contractual payout $200.000m, equal to $0.99 per diluted share and 1.3% of $15,235m base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any earnout obligation not represented in future OE cash outflows should be deducted as a non-common-equity claim in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The initial cash consideration paid for LesserEvil totaled $ 769,090 and consisted of cash on hand and short-term borrowings; however, the Company may be required to pay additional contingent consideration ranging from zero to a maximum of $ 200,000 if certain defined earnings targets are met over a multi-year period.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge does not separately show the earnout, and the latest carrying value is unresolved. Even the filed contractual maximum would reduce base value by only $0.99 per share, versus the $97.87 gap between the $75.28 base value and $173.15 market price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 28, 2026 LesserEvil contingent-consideration carrying value and expected payout; confirm whether it is already represented in projected OE, and otherwise deduct that amount without changing operating assumptions.

audit_findings.title: Separately added stakes may double-count tax-credit investment returns
audit_findings.magnitude: filed 2025 tax credits and related benefits of $34.419m less $24.483m investment write-down equals a $9.936m net benefit; if fully retained in anchor OE, computed base-value effect is approximately $139.6m or $0.69 per share; stakes balance is $174.834m
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining income, tax credits or investee results in OE while separately adding the related investment balance capitalizes the return and also credits the underlying asset.
audit_findings.evidence: The tax credits, when realized, are recognized as a reduction of tax expense under the flow-through method, at which time the corresponding equity investment is written-down to reflect the remaining value of the future benefits to be realized.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not prove that the returns were retained, so double counting remains a possibility rather than a demonstrated error. The identifiable 2025 net tax-credit benefit would represent about 0.9% of base equity value if fully capitalized, and the entire separately added stake balance is only 1.1% of base equity value; neither scale can change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $174.834m balance by investment and trace 2025 tax credits, write-downs and investee earnings through OE; remove any retained net return or remove the corresponding bridge asset, then document the immaterial sensitivity.

audit_findings.title: The denominator treats two classes with unequal distribution rights as identical claims
audit_findings.magnitude: computed hypothetical two-class allocation would increase listed-common value by approximately 2.52%, or $1.89 from the $75.28 base value; filed Class B conversion is one-for-one
audit_findings.mechanism: A two-class allocation would weight listed Common shares more heavily for their 10% dividend preference, while a fully converted calculation divides equity across one-for-one common equivalents.
audit_findings.evidence: With respect to dividend rights, the Common Stock holders are entitled to cash dividends 10 % higher than those declared and paid on the Class B Common Stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing expressly permits Class B conversion into Common Stock one-for-one at any time and uses that treatment for diluted Common EPS, supporting the valuation's fully converted denominator. Even ignoring conversion and allocating value solely by the current dividend ratio would raise base value only to about $77.17, still far below $173.15.
audit_findings.action: Document that the denominator is intentionally fully converted and reconcile its Common, Class B and dilutive-security components; rerun a two-class allocation only if governing documents show a substantive restriction on one-for-one conversion or different residual rights.

audit_findings.title: All cash may not be distributable without a tax leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified tax leakage; maximum affected bridge balance $791.213m, equal to $3.91 per diluted share and 5.2% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Withholding or repatriation tax reduces the realizable value of cash and short-term investments separately added in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We intend to continue to reinvest the remainder of the earnings outside of the United States for which there would be a material tax implication to distributing for the foreseeable future and, therefore, have not recognized additional tax expense on these earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that a substantial majority of cash is held abroad but also says a majority is distributable without material tax. The taxable portion and rate are not supplied. Even the deliberately extreme assumption that the entire $791.213m balance had no equity value would reduce base value only from $75.28 to about $71.37, leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged; actual leakage must be smaller than that ceiling.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 28, 2026 cash/STI schedule by jurisdiction, distributable basis and applicable withholding or repatriation tax; apply the supported tax haircut to the affected portion of the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2017 $26.9m, FY2021 $32.2m, FY2022 $45.7m and FY2023 $65.4m; $0 direct effect on the stated 2025 anchor from those historical amounts, while FY2025 is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any eligible non-economic D&A left as an expense understates OE; only a 2025 classification would directly change the latest-year anchor, while earlier amounts could affect trend evidence but the trend is already above the MIN-rule anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2017 $26.9m (10.3% of filed D&A); FY2021 $32.2m (10.2% of filed D&A); FY2022 $45.7m (12.1% of filed D&A); FY2023 $65.4m (15.6% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The conservative treatment cannot overstate value. The disclosed historical residuals do not alter the $1,015.6m anchor because the model uses latest 2025 OE and fixed scenario growth, but the record supplies no 2025 residual classification. A comparable 2025 omission may affect value, yet its amount and eligibility cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile filed 2025 D&A by PP&E depreciation, acquired-intangible amortization, software amortization, leases and other components; rerun only for the documented eligible 2025 add-back, with corresponding maintenance investment preserved.
